title: Two new PhD students join the lab
description:
The LUNAR Lab is excited to welcome two outstanding incoming PhD students: Maya Chen and Oren Friedman. Both will begin their doctoral studies in the fall semester and have already been collaborating with the lab on early-stage projects.

Maya joins us from UC Berkeley, where she completed her undergraduate thesis on grounded language acquisition in embodied agents. Her doctoral research at LUNAR will focus on how distributional semantics interacts with perceptual grounding — investigating whether language models that have never seen the world can nonetheless develop representations that mirror the conceptual structure found in human cognition.

Oren comes from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, where he worked on cross-lingual transfer and morphological generalization. At LUNAR, Oren will pursue questions at the intersection of interpretability and linguistic theory, with a particular focus on how syntactic knowledge is encoded and distributed across layers in large transformer models.

Both students were selected through a highly competitive process from an applicant pool of over 300 candidates. We are grateful to our funding sources — including a recent NSF award — which make it possible to support graduate researchers doing fundamental science.

Welcome to the lab, Maya and Oren. We can't wait to see where your research takes us.
